context: Finally, we observe that an OR decision tree with low total cost can be “unrolled” into a plain decision tree of low depth: we can replace every disjunction of width w by a plain decision tree of depth w that queries the same variables and computes their OR. (In general, any function on w variables can be computed by a decision tree of depth w.) B Claim 4.6. Let T be an OR decision tree where all paths have total cost at most d. Then there exists a (plain) decision tree of depth d that computes the same function as T .
